record.paper_title: The Critical Beta-splitting Random Tree II: Overview and Open Problems
record.context_brief: Hidden symmetry in the growth process
record.original_question: In the n→∞ inductive growth picture for CTCS(n), let p↑ be the limiting probability that a new leaf is added by branch extension and let p↗ be the limiting probability of a side-bud extension. Explain whether the observed identity p↑ = p↗ can be derived from an underlying symmetry of the tree shape or the growth dynamics.

Open Problem 20 Is the fact p↑ = p↗ a consequence of some kind of symmetry for the shape of the tree?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the critical beta-splitting random tree model defined as follows. For an integer m ≥ 2, a clade of m leaves is recursively partitioned into two sub-clades of sizes i and m−i (1 ≤ i ≤ m−1) with probability proportional to 1/(i(m−i)); recursion stops at clades of size 1. This produces a random rooted binary tree CTCS(n) on n labeled leaves. The family {CTCS(n) : n ≥ 2} is consistent under the operation "delete a uniformly random leaf and contract the resulting degree-2 vertex," and therefore admits an inductive growth construction: CTCS(n+1) is obtained from CTCS(n) by inserting one new leaf according to a prescribed conditional distribution.

In this growth construction, classify the insertion of the new leaf into one of three local types:
 • branch extension: the new leaf is attached so that one bud of an existing terminal cherry is replaced by a new branch ending in a pair of buds;
 • side-bud addition: the new leaf is attached as a side-bud in the interior of an existing edge;
 • side-bud extension: an existing side-bud is replaced by a new branch with two terminal buds.

Let p↑, p→, and p↗ denote, respectively, the limiting (as n → ∞) probabilities of these three event types at the step from CTCS(n) to CTCS(n+1). It is observed that p↑ = p↗.

Determine whether the identity p↑ = p↗ can be derived as a consequence of some intrinsic symmetry of the random tree shape or of the growth dynamics, and if so exhibit such a symmetry.
artifact.status_search_result: The question appears as an open problem in the overview of the critical beta-splitting random tree model (2023). Subsequent papers in the series (2024–2025) on the exchangeable partition representation, fringe tree, leaf-height Mellin analysis, and contraction methods extend the theory but do not announce a resolution of this particular identity via symmetry. No search result indicates that p↑ = p↗ has been explained by an established symmetry of the tree shape or the growth dynamics.
